text: The Isle of Man is an insular Celtic site. Irish sailors settled the small island between Britain and Ireland in the fourth or fifth century C.E. They named it after the Irish sea god Manannán mac Lir. Boat travel to the island was hazardous, so the Manx language slowly divided from its parent Irish. The islanders were fierce sailors. In ancient times their realm included the Hebrides, which Scotland took at the battle of Largs in 1263. The island kept a long-running parliament named the Tynwald. Regular boat service began in the 1830s and the Manx language declined before English. The last native Manx speaker died in 1974 at the age of 74.
objective: Document the Isle of Man, its Celtic settlement and its naming after Manannán mac Lir.
